question: Which f-block element in the periodic table is represented by the Greek symbol 'alpha' and the metallic 'rays'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Actinium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Actinium:-**

 
 
• **The f-block element represented by the Greek symbol 'alpha' and the metallic 'rays' is Actinium, which has the atomic number 89 and belongs to the group 3 of the periodic table.**
 
• Actinium is a radioactive element that was discovered in 1899 by Andrundefined-Louis Debierne and named after the Greek word 'aktinos', meaning ray or beam, due to its high radioactivity.
 
• Actinium is a silvery-white metal that tarnishes in air and reacts with water and acids. It has no stable isotopes and its most stable isotope, Actinium-227, has a half-life of 21.8 years.
 
• Actinium is used in nuclear medicine for cancer treatment and as a neutron source in scientific research. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lanthanum:-**

 
 
• It is a soft, silvery-white metal that belongs to the lanthanide series and is used in the production of high-refractive-index glass, as well as in catalysts, electrodes, and other applications.
 
 
 
• **Rhenium:-**
 
 
• It is a dense, silvery-white metal that belongs to the group 7 of the periodic table and is used in high-temperature alloys, thermocouples, and catalysts.
 
 
 
• **Tungsten:-**
 
 
• It is a hard, dense, gray metal that belongs to the group 6 of the periodic table and is used in filaments, electrical contacts, and other applications.
